sourceOfTruth: assembled runtime IDs in src/ngnQuestionBank.ts plus source inventory and this ledger

runtimeInventory.verificationMethod: At run start, re-read src/questionBank.ts and src/ngnQuestionBank.ts at e0c765620ce434dbe083f5770d04587e46ea9be8. Source-level assembly exports 500 core items (36 case-study screens, 100 curated traditional items, 364 category-generated remainder), asserts 500 entries and 500 unique core IDs, then assembles 100 NGN extension items into questionBank600 and asserts 600 unique IDs with cross-bank normalized prompt/scenario guards. The 364 authored rewrite records replace existing IDs and contribute zero net-new inventory. This audit-only run did not execute the runtime build/tests.

baselineAudit.notes: Static triage only. 140/244 items in the third rewrite tranche are classified for substantive revision and qualified educator review; no clinical approval or content changes were recorded.

commonFindings: All 20 are single-response items built from the same topic-substituted reassessment prompt/task; four option families and four corresponding rationale families are each reused five times.

Most named neurologic and musculoskeletal topics lack defining history, injury/procedure context, focused assessment, diagnostic evidence or treatment timeline. The seizure-precautions item has a new seizure and sodium 118 mEq/L, and the delirium item has new confusion, but neither has a topic-specific task or defensible targeted response.

Unrelated acute findings compete with the named topics: potassium 6.2 mEq/L with peaked T waves, glucose 42 mg/dL with unsafe swallowing, sodium 118 mEq/L with seizure, hypoxemia/hypercapnia, bleeding/coagulopathy, falling hemoglobin and renal/perfusion deterioration.

Unsupported or incomplete context includes a newborn assigned subarachnoid hemorrhage, open tibial fracture and neurovascular compromise; a child assigned MS exacerbation and stroke dysphagia; and postoperative status without a documented relevant procedure for spinal cord injury or hip dislocation.

All 20 have four options and four option rationales; the answer index matches the option rationale marked Correct. This structural consistency does not establish a clinically defensible topic-specific key; distractors and rationales remain generic.

CJMM labels rotate evenly across four steps (five items each), but the task is unchanged and does not distinguish recognize, analyze, prioritize or take-action performance. Objective and Client Needs subcategory metadata are absent.
The source helper marks the records development/generated/not-clinically-verified/draft with empty references. The runtime migration is structural only; no clinical review is implied.

No exact duplicate IDs occur within the inspected 20. Prompt/task, option and rationale patterns are near-duplicate templates. No content, answer key, ID, learner history, pool membership or review metadata was changed.
